continuity.opening: Pinocchio and Lamp-Wick have become donkeys after surrendering themselves to Toyland.
continuity.closing: Swallowed by the Terrible Shark, Pinocchio leaves the hopeless Tunny and follows a mysterious light.
continuity.next: The light inside the Shark leads Pinocchio to the father he has spent so long trying to find.

learningObjective: Explain exploitation, consequence, and renewed agency using cause-and-effect links, contrast, and emotionally controlled narration.

beats.title: Sold at the Market
beats.purpose: Reveal the hidden business behind Toyland and separate the two transformed friends.

beats.title: The Circus's New Star
beats.purpose: Show Pinocchio being trained and displayed as an obedient product.

beats.title: The Fairy in the Audience
beats.purpose: Turn a glittering performance into a painful attempt to reach the Fairy.

beats.title: Worth Four Coins
beats.purpose: Connect Pinocchio's distraction and injury to another owner's cold calculation.

beats.title: Beneath the Donkey Skin
beats.purpose: Move through the sea ordeal into the restoration of Pinocchio's wooden form.

beats.title: The Blue Goat
beats.purpose: Give Pinocchio a brief taste of freedom and a visible sign of the Fairy's care.

beats.title: The Terrible Shark
beats.purpose: Overwhelm the hopeful escape with the scale and force of a new danger.

beats.title: A Light in the Dark
beats.purpose: Contrast the Tunny's resignation with Pinocchio's newly purposeful courage.
